text:
sam: noticing p95 jitter on host-rack-77 (eu-north-1). affected fractional dedicated slices; looks correlated with a spike from tenant Q around 06:20 UTC.

priya: saw the alert. grafana graph: https://grafana/redwood/d/egress?var-host=host-rack-77&from=now-2h

michael: can you paste ethtool and /proc/interrupts snapshot? suspect VF IRQ contention again.

sam: quick dumps:
```
ethtool -S eth2 | egrep "vf[0-3]|tx_errors|rx_dropped"
eth2_vf0_tx_packets: 1.8M
eth2_vf0_tx_errors: 0
eth2_vf1_tx_packets: 160k
eth2_vf1_rx_drops: 34
/proc/interrupts (snippet):
  72:  220000  430000  13000 PCI-MSI eth2-Tx-vf0
  73:    9000   12000    800 PCI-MSI eth2-Tx-vf1
  74:  450000  120000  30000 PCI-MSI eth2-Rx
```

sam: vf0 is tenant Q. bursts line up with their nightly fanout job. vf1 consumers see rx_drops and their p95 jumps.

leah: infra-bot: opened INC-9123 and notified oncall. :rotating_light:

ops-bot: [AUDIT] INC-9123 created by sam (priority P2).

priya: mitigation options: 1) ephemeral steer tenant Q to spare-fractional-eu-north (costly), 2) apply temporary per-vf egress throttle on vf0, 3) flip IRQ affinity, 4) mark host as vf-sensitive to avoid new multi-tenant VFs. Thoughts?

michael: I'd do (2) + (4) immediately. Throttle is cheap and fast. Steer if throttle fails. Flipping IRQ affinity is riskier live.

sam: command for throttle I plan to run:
```
# cap vf0 to 250mbit for 30m
tc qdisc replace dev vf0 root tbf rate 250mbit burst 64k latency 100ms
```

leah: tagging @costs-bot: spare-fractional-eu-north is ~x3 cost. If throttle fails we'll need approval for steer.

costs-bot: acknowledged. Estimated incremental cost for 30m steer: $1.20.

priya: also add telemetry hook to log per-slice KV cache regen events every 10s so we can correlate if regen amplifies the burst.

michael: running throttle now and capturing pcap + irq snapshot. infra-bot: post audit.

ops-bot: [AUDIT] tc throttle applied by michael on vf0 rate=250mbit TTL=1800

sam: initial observation T+2m: p95 for vf1 consumers dropped ~45%. rx_drops on eth2 reduced. Looks promising.

leah: long-term item: consider scheduler change to prefer 1:1 VF-to-slice on hosts labeled 'vf-sensitive' and add auto-label when vf_rx_drops > 20 in 5m. That would reduce packing density but avoid repeated steers.

michael: agree. I'll open a PR to add host-label heuristics and a placement penalty. We'll simulate impact on bin-packing before rolling out.

priya: ops-runbook update: "If per-vf rx_drops > 20 in 5m and neighbor p95 regresses -> 1) apply per-vf throttle 2) monitor 10m 3) if unstable, steer offender -> spare pool 4) attach pcap/irqs to incident and tag host vf-sensitive if recurring 3x in 7d."

costs-bot: FYI: if we label 5% of hosts vf-sensitive and require looser packing, estimated OPEX increase ~+$8k/mo. Will provide simulation for other percentages.

sam: good. For now throttle held and SLOs recovered. Leaving TTL 30m and will re-evaluate. attaching pcap/irq dump to INC-9123. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
